UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.Purpose: Keep abstracts, snippets, summaries, and inaccessible citations from counting as inspected full text when unseen methods, harms, subgroups, comparators, outcomes, funding, conflicts, or limitations could change the conclusion.
UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.Activation: Mandatory for study-heavy safety reviews, treatment comparisons, guideline audits, controversial claims, quantitative-risk disputes, diagnostic-method reviews, protocol appraisals, evidence-absence claims, and any structured or deep question where an inaccessible study's full text could materially change the conclusion. Not for emergency triage, simple definitions, low-stakes quick answers, pure brainstorming, or when supplied full-text evidence already suffices and no inaccessible source is decision-critical.
UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.Rule: A source is decision-critical when inspecting its methods, tables, appendices, adverse events, baseline characteristics, allocation, co-interventions, endpoint definitions, patient-level results, attrition, or conflicts could materially change whether human evidence exists; the direction, magnitude, consistency, or certainty of benefit or harm; whether a result applies to the exact population, route, formulation, dose, timing, comparator, component, bundle, schedule, program, or endpoint; whether apparently favorable or unfavorable outcomes reflect comparator misclassification, predecessor-lineage debt, adverse-event filtering, selection, confounding, historical controls, or reporting; or whether an absence, safety, or clinical-action conclusion is permitted. Build a prioritized citation map of direct human, close proxy, mechanistic, review, and safety sources that identifies the decision-changing full texts, and triage each inaccessible source as decision-critical, useful but noncritical, or peripheral, with a one-sentence reason.

Classify each prioritized source's access as full text inspected; auditable full-text extraction inspected; partial text; abstract only; snippet or secondary description only; identified but inaccessible; or identity unresolved. Never merge these states.

When a decision-critical source lacks full text or an auditable full-text extraction, first automatically try supported lawful repository routes and DOI-based open-access resolution. A resolver location is not inspected full text until the linked document is fetched, identity-checked, version-labeled, and checked for completeness. On AskRigor connector runs the server enforces this chain: acquire_open_full_text, continue_open_full_text until exhausted, then validate_study_method_audit or validate_review_method_audit, which refuse unless the full text was read to exhaustion; finalize_research requires a validated audit receipt for each key study or an acquisition receipt proving a lead.
If access still fails, record the exact studies in priority order, verified identifiers when available, why each may change the decision, the fields still unresolved, and the claim-local uncertainty. Offer a lawful user upload, library route, or authorized external-service handoff only when materially useful, in batches of about three to ten studies (fewer for dense trials, old scans, or complex safety reports), and extract in batches of that size. Failure to obtain it never freezes unrelated executable research or justifies treating unseen content as evidence.

An abstract, search-result snippet, review summary, AI synthesis, book paraphrase, or public webpage does not satisfy a decision-critical full-text requirement. Do not infer unreported methods, denominators, adverse events, baseline severity, allocation, co-interventions, subgroup definitions, follow-up, funding, or limitations.

While a decision-critical full text remains inaccessible, only the claims it could materially affect must remain unresolved or provisional. A bounded synthesis may use the sources actually inspected and must identify the inaccessible paper as a possibly useful research lead, state which methods, results, tables, harms, or other details remain unseen, and explain what could change. Do not infer a likely direction of bias without evidence.
Do not mark the whole answer partial solely because one lawful full text cannot be obtained. Full-scope completion still requires all executable applicable work and honest claim-local boundaries; an inaccessible source never counts as inspected evidence and cannot support a class-wide comparison or ranking. If the user declines acquisition, an authorized external service is unavailable, or lawful access fails, do not repeatedly block a bounded answer: continue other executable research, give the best claim-bounded synthesis, identify the missing studies and unresolved fields, and lower confidence only for conclusions the missing information could affect.

After each batch, verify study identity, internal consistency, exact comparator composition and lineage, raw counts, denominators, analysis population, endpoint definitions, adjustments, component-to-program scope, effect measures, confounders, subgroup logic, adverse-event capture and relatedness adjudication, funding, conflicts, intent claims, missing fields, overclaims, and extraction completeness. Keep a running ledger of completed studies, unresolved discrepancies, missing full texts, direct versus proxy evidence, decision-critical status, and next-batch priority. Stop when more full texts are unlikely to change the decision, the planned direct evidence is exhausted, the user explicitly accepts a provisional answer, or access limits require a clearly labeled partial synthesis. Before synthesis, rerun the QuantitativeRiskAndResearchAudit and the applicable-module ledger across the combined evidence, and write the answer only from verified extraction and clearly labeled supplementary evidence.
UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.EscalationRequestMinimum: An upload or extraction request lists the prioritized studies with full citation and verified DOI, PMID, registry ID, ISBN-linked chapter, or other identifier when available; why each is decision-critical; current access status; exact pages, tables, appendices, or chapters sought when known; the extraction fields needed; which conclusions are provisional and how each source could change them; and suggested batch size and order.
UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.ExtractionMinimum: Extract the full citation and verified identifier; access status and extraction provenance; design and setting; enrolled, randomized, exposed, completed, and analyzed sample sizes; inclusion, exclusion, baseline severity, geography, treatment history, and co-interventions; intervention dose, route, form, timing, frequency, and duration; exact comparator class, composition, route, schedule, background care, rescue therapy, allocation method, and blinding; comparator ancestry, predecessor evidence, independently characterized baseline, and unresolved baseline evidence debt; whether the evidence concerns a component, complete product, bundle, sequence, cumulative schedule, or program; exact primary and secondary endpoint definitions and endpoint-layer match; raw event counts, denominators, absolute and relative effects, and uncertainty intervals; observed versus modeled results; solicited and unsolicited adverse events, serious adverse events, all versus related events, risk windows, relatedness criteria and adjudication, discontinuations, post-withdrawal capture, and follow-up; adjustment variables and important omitted confounders; funding, conflicts, sponsor role, registration, and deviations; and author-stated and auditor-identified limitations. For historical or multilingual sources add edition, date, author or compiler, textual stratum, original versus quoted or reconstructed status, original-language passage, translation uncertainty, and dependent citation lineage; for historical interventions add source material, species or part, processing, preparation, co-ingredients, route, original dose unit, period-specific conversion uncertainty, and batch-versus-administered-dose context.
UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.AccessBoundary: Use lawful access: check user uploads and accessible libraries, and use open-access repositories, author manuscripts, publisher access, institutional subscriptions, lawful borrowing, or direct author contact. Never provide, recommend, or chase pirate or shadow-library links. A user-approved external extractor retrieves and extracts explicitly reported full-text details only; it is not an authority, does not adjudicate conclusions, and cannot substitute for audit.
